title: Inverse-image relabelling identifies completed coefficient reduction towers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme isomorphism $g:X\to Y$ on schemes where $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Put $R_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $F=g^{-1}$ be the inverse-image equivalence on module sheaves transported along the coefficient isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}:g^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X$ defined as the composite $g^{-1}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_mg^{-1}(A_{E,m})_Y\xrightarrow{\varprojlim_mc^g_{A_{E,m}}}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_X$ using [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex of $R_Y$-module sheaves whose terms are flat [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and for $n\geq1$ put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y$, with tensor complexes as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $\pi_{n,Y}:R_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ for the limit projections and $\rho_{n,Y}:(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ for the coefficient reductions, and similarly on $X$. The quotient and transition arrows are $\gamma_n:x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $\tau_n=1\otimes\rho_{n,Y}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]; resolution comparisons mean the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]. For every $n\geq1$ there is a natural identification $$\beta_n:F(P_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P)\otimes_{R_X}(A_{E,n})_X,$$ namely the termwise tensor isomorphism $F(P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,n})_Y)\cong F(P)\otimes_{F R_Y}F(A_{E,n})_Y$ of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] followed by the change of coefficients along $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $c^g_{A_{E,n}}$, which is well defined because of the coefficient-projection square $\pi_{n,X}\circ c_{\mathcal O_E}=c^g_{A_{E,n}}\circ F(\pi_{n,Y})$; on local sections $\beta_n(F(x\otimes a))=F(x)\otimes c^g_{A_{E,n}}(F(a))$. Under these identifications $F(\gamma_n)$ and $F(\tau_n)$ are the quotient map $F(P)\to F(P)\otimes_{R_X}(A_{E,n})_X$, $y\mapsto y\otimes1$, and the transition map $1\otimes\rho_{n,X}$ for $F(P)$, i.e., writing $\gamma^X_n,\tau^X_n$ for these maps, $\beta_n F(\gamma_n)=\gamma^X_n$ and $\beta_nF(\tau_n)=\tau^X_n\beta_{n+1}$; the $\beta_n$ are natural in chain maps $P\to P'$ of such complexes. Finally, let $q:P\to K$ and $q':P'\to K$ be quasi-isomorphisms from two such complexes $P,P'$ to a complex $K$ of $R_Y$-modules such that $F(P)$ and $F(P')$ are K-flat complexes of $R_X$-modules, with comparison isomorphism $\theta_n:P_n\to P'_n$ of [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] and $\beta'_n$ the identification for $P'$; then $\beta'_n\circ F(\theta_n)=\theta^X_n\circ\beta_n$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, where $\theta^X_n$ is the comparison isomorphism of that lemma for the quasi-isomorphisms $F(q),F(q'):F(P),F(P')\to F(K)$.

source.place: Statement, coefficient-object paragraph beginning “For a coefficient ring”: completed integral coefficient sheaf. Agent lemma extracted from step 4 of lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback for the canonical Weil-structure comparison, via def-weil-constant-weil-structure; the blueprint does not state this lemma.

proof.text: Write $B_{n,W}=(A_{E,n})_W$ and $c_n=c^g_{A_{E,n}}$. By clauses (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], inverse image preserves the limit defining $R_Y$ and each $c_n$ is a ring isomorphism. Naturality there, applied to $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$, gives $\rho_{n,X}c_{n+1}=c_n g^{-1}(\rho_{n,Y})$. Thus the maps $c_n g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})$ form a cone to the tower on $X$. The composite defining $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ has these components, by the projection characterization of the canonical limit comparison. Consequently $\pi_{n,X}c_{\mathcal O_E}=c_n g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})$. The limit of the $c_n$ is invertible: the $c_n^{-1}$ form the inverse cone and the two composites have identity projections. Together with the limit comparison this proves that the specified $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits: module sheaves) and Tag 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves: abelian sheaves). The ring-sheaf projection calculation is the universal-property argument written in this step, using the canonical limit comparison and ring-map naturality stated in lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image; neither tag is a theorem about limits of ring sheaves.

proof.text: Apply the tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] in degree $i$ with $\mathcal O=R_Y$, $\mathcal F=P^i$, $\mathcal G=B_{n,Y}$. Transport scalars by $c_{\mathcal O_E}$ and $c_n$. The resulting map sends $g^{-1}x\otimes a$ to $g^{-1}x\otimes c_n(a)$. It respects the balanced relation: for $r\in g^{-1}R_Y$, the images of $(r g^{-1}x)\otimes a$ and $g^{-1}x\otimes g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})(r)a$ coincide since $\pi_{n,X}(c_{\mathcal O_E}(r))=c_n(g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})(r))$ by Step 1. Its inverse uses $c_n^{-1}$ on the second factor and the inverse tensor comparison. These maps respect restrictions; the sheaf tensor product of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] therefore gives mutually inverse module maps. This constructs precisely the stated $\beta_n$ and its prescribed local formula.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), balancing and coefficient transport written explicitly

proof.text: The coefficient sheaf $B_{n,Y}$ is a complex concentrated in degree zero. Hence the total tensor convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] makes $d_{P_n}^i=d_P^i\otimes1$. Naturality of the tensor comparison of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] with respect to $d_P^i$ gives $\beta_n^{i+1}F(d_P^i\otimes1)=(F(d_P^i)\otimes1)\beta_n^i$. Thus the termwise maps in Step 2 and their inverses are chain maps, giving an isomorphism of complexes. There is no interchange with an infinite totalization here, since only one coefficient degree is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 06YL (section-flat), tensor total differential with one factor in degree zero

proof.text: The constant-sheaf ring isomorphism $c_n$ is unital. The local formula in Step 2 therefore sends $F(x\otimes1)$ to $F(x)\otimes1$, which proves $\beta_n F(\gamma_n)=\gamma_n^X$. This is an equality of $R_X$-module chain maps: the action on the coefficient factor is through $\pi_{n,X}$ by Step 1. The map $\gamma_n$ is exactly the quotient arrow specified in [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. The equality is verified on the presheaf pure tensors defining [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], then passes to their sheafification; the section formula in clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies the inverse-image sections used here.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); the unit calculation for the quotient map

proof.text: For a local tensor $F(x\otimes a)$ at level $n+1$, the two maps $\beta_nF(\tau_n)$ and $\tau_n^X\beta_{n+1}$ give, respectively, $F(x)\otimes c_n(F(\rho_{n,Y})(F(a)))$ and $F(x)\otimes\rho_{n,X}(c_{n+1}(F(a)))$. These agree by the coefficient-reduction naturality equation in Step 1, an instance of clause (3) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Since $\tau_n$ is $1\otimes\rho_{n,Y}$ by [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], the universal property of the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] proves $\beta_nF(\tau_n)=\tau_n^X\beta_{n+1}$. Both are maps of $R_X$-complexes after restricting level $n+1$ and level $n$ along their projections; no assertion of $B_{n+1,X}$-linearity with its original action on the level-$n$ source is needed.

Let $u:P\to P'$ be a chain map and put $u_n=u\otimes1$. Degreewise tensor naturality in [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] gives $\beta'_nF(u_n)=(F(u)\otimes1)\beta_n$; equivalently both send $F(x\otimes a)$ to $F(u(x))\otimes c_n(F(a))$. Step 3 shows these are chain maps. This proves the requested chain-map naturality, and also applies to the auxiliary K-flat flat-term complexes introduced below.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), functoriality in the first factor

proof.text: The underlying abelian-sheaf inverse image is exact by clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Transport of the scalar action by a ring isomorphism changes neither the underlying abelian sheaf nor its maps. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this inverse image is exact also on $R_Y$-modules with target $R_X$-modules, and on $B_{n,Y}$-modules with target $B_{n,X}$-modules. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to these exact functors. Thus termwise $F$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induces the derived functors denoted $F$ below; in particular $F(q)$ and $F(q')$ really are quasi-isomorphisms. Additivity also sends a chain homotopy $h$ to $F(h)$, since it preserves the identity $u-v=dh+hd$.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); module exactness uses the underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels

proof.text: Apply the right-hand (MS2) assertion of [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated] to $q:P\to K$ and $q':P'\to K$ in the homotopy category. It gives $t:V\to P'$ a quasi-isomorphism and $v:V\to P$ with $qv=q't$. Two-out-of-three in the same node makes $v$ a quasi-isomorphism. Choose a K-flat resolution $r:T\to V$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $a=vr:T\to P$, $b=tr:T\to P'$, choosing chain representatives. Both are quasi-isomorphisms and $qa=q'b$ in the homotopy category. For the ringed-topos morphism with structure map $c_{\mathcal O_E}$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] makes $g^*T=g^{-1}T\otimes_{g^{-1}R_Y}R_X$ K-flat with flat terms. The normalized scalar-isomorphism comparison of [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] identifies this complex with $F(T)$, so $F(T)$ is K-flat. Its maps $F(a),F(b)$ are quasi-isomorphisms by Step 7. The hypotheses that $F(P),F(P')$ are K-flat are precisely the remaining K-flat hypotheses for the comparison on $X$.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); derived.tex Tag 05RT; sites-modules.tex Tag 03CZ

proof.text: Put $T_n=T\otimes_{R_Y}B_{n,Y}$, $a_n=a\otimes1$, $b_n=b\otimes1$. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes $a_n,b_n$ quasi-isomorphisms. To identify the canonical comparison, write $L=L\pi_{n,Y}^*$ and let $\varepsilon_Z:L(QZ)\to Q(Z\otimes B_{n,Y})$ be the natural comparison of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. It is invertible for $Z=T,P,P'$ by the K-flat computations of the change-of-rings node. Naturality gives $[a_n]\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_P L([a])$ and $[b_n]\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_{P'}L([b])$. The computation at $q$ is $c_q=\varepsilon_P L([q])^{-1}$ and that at $q'$ is $c_{q'}=\varepsilon_{P'} L([q'])^{-1}$. Since $[q][a]=[q'][b]$, cancellation yields $c_{q'}c_q^{-1}=[b_n][a_n]^{-1}$. This is $\theta_n$ as defined in [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]. The same calculation on $X$, using Step 8 and the assumed K-flatness of $F(P),F(P')$, gives $\theta_n^X=[F(b)\otimes1][F(a)\otimes1]^{-1}$. The invoked change-of-rings functor on the homotopy category is exact by the cited node, and its comparison $\varepsilon$ is the one computing that derived functor; thus no comparison between unspecified choices is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), natural computation maps; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YT and 06YY

proof.text:
Apply Step 6 to $a:T\to P$ and $b:T\to P'$ and write $a_n^X=F(a)\otimes1$, $b_n^X=F(b)\otimes1$. In the finite-coefficient derived category on $X$ it gives $\beta_nF([a_n])=[a_n^X]\beta_n^T$ and $\beta'_nF([b_n])=[b_n^X]\beta_n^T$. The arrows $[a_n]$ and $[a_n^X]$ are invertible by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; $F([a_n])$ is invertible because $F$ is a functor by Step 7. Using the comparison formulas of Step 9, the desired equation is the cancellation
$$\beta'_nF(\theta_n)=\beta'_nF([b_n])F([a_n])^{-1}=[b_n^X]\beta_n^TF([a_n])^{-1}=[b_n^X][a_n^X]^{-1}\beta_n=\theta_n^X\beta_n.$$
This proves compatibility with the canonical resolution comparisons, in the asserted $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, and completes all clauses.
